question.text: In 'Options on Futures,' when a long call position is exercised, it devolves into:

answer.text: A long position in the underlying futures contract at the strike price
Direct physical delivery of the commodity
Cash settlement at the spot price
A short position in the underlying futures contract

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook devolvement mapping: Long call -> long futures, Long put -> short futures, Short call -> short futures, Short put -> long futures. The devolved futures position is opened at the option's strike price. The Trap: Direct physical delivery is the mechanism for Options on Goods, not Options on Futures. Cash settlement at spot is not the devolvement route. A short futures position would result from exercising a long put, not a long call. Note: Once devolved, the futures position is subject to standard futures margin requirements and may be cash settled or delivered depending on the relevant futures contract.
